newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA PROPOSES TO LEVEL TAX RULES.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA PROPOSES TO LEVEL TAX RULES.

text.p: The Lithuanian government said on Wednesday that it would seek amendments to the country's tax regulations to level the playing field between companies with domestic and foreign capital.

"It is suggested to stop giving tax advantages to companies in which foreign capital will be invested. According to European Union directives all companies should enjoy equal principles," the government said in a statement.
Companies which have had advantages under Lithuania's foreign investment law will continue to have this right, the government said.

Lithuanian law currently states that if foreign investment exceeds $2 million, companies are exempt from profit tax for a period of three years and for the next three years pay only 50 percent profit tax.
The government also proposed a zero tax tariff on profits used for investments, the government said.
"Profit tax is 29 percent but the profit tax used for investment is to be taxed with a zero tariff," it said.
